summary: Steel tower, 30 m (98 ft), built 2014 per Alberta Wildfire's layer; active with fly access. A news report names lakes of the same name; no source describes the site today.

access.note: Active, staffed Alberta Wildfire lookout. The layer codes access mode as fly. No source found says the public may visit.

events.note: Present steel tower, per the Alberta Wildfire lookout layer

evidence.supports: steel tower, 30 m tall, elevation 784 m, present structure built 2014
steel introduced in the 1920s and increasingly replaced wood
evidence.quote: Introduced in the 1920s, steel increasingly replaced wood for tower construction.

evidence.supports: observer's job: spot fires, identify them and report where they are, for over a century
evidence.quote: Detection, identification and then communication of the whereabouts of fires has been the job of the seasonal fire lookout observer in Alberta for over a hundred years.

evidence.supports: lakes named Otter Lakes north of Little Buffalo, about 30 km ENE of Red Earth Creek; place name only, not linked to the tower
evidence.quote: Otter Lakes are located north of Little Buffalo, or about 30 kilometres ENE of Red Earth Creek.

evidence.supports: 127 wildfire lookout sites; each staffed by an observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: 127 wildfire lookout sites are located throughout Alberta's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: sites isolated; staff must be ready for a curious bear
evidence.quote: Wildfire lookout sites are isolated and the staff that work them must be prepared for a wide range of possibilities, including an encounter with a curious bear.

notes_for_editor: Facts come from the provincial layer (record OL, location verified) and the general Alberta.ca and RETROactive pages. The Lakeside Leader page is undated in the cached text and reports lightning fires near Otter Lakes in a June storm. It does not mention the lookout, so no fire event is recorded and the report is used only for the place name. Neither the Lakeside Leader page nor any other source found ties the tower to that location. No source describes the site today beyond the layer's active status. No photos, staffing history or register entries found.
